decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt To conclude, the key finding that individuals evaluate those who palter and those who lie by commission as being equally unethical was successfully replicated. In the original study, the contrast between the paltering and lying conditions in simple linear regression assessing the effect of condition on ratings of the unethicality of the Buyer indicated a non-significant p-value (p = .91); this p-value was also non-significant in the present replication (p = .90).
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: rogers2017.html, line 727 (Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt); raw_data.csv, line 377
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding record the replication outcome for Rogers et al. (2017) Study 3 (project rogers2017) as 'successful' (the blind coder omitted the quote from the included primary report). The attached primary replication report (rogers2017.html, line 727) and raw_data.csv (line 377, replicated_instructor_code = 1, replicated_report_code = 1) confirm that the replication succeeded across both the focal contrast between paltering and lying on Buyer unethicality (b = 0.04378, SE = 0.35011, p = .90065) and the contrasts showing that honest Buyers were rated significantly more ethical, more trustworthy, and more likely to be engaged in future negotiations than Buyers who paltered or lied.

decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT FILE: raw_data.csv, line 326 (project nook2017)
decisions.reason: For Nook, Schleider, & Somerville (2017) Study 1 (project nook2017), no primary replication report is included in the supplied source (replication_report_included = no). In raw_data.csv (line 326), the single extracted statistic is in the same direction and statistically significant (t(1101.9) = 3.5641, N = 56, same_dir = yes, vs. original t(106) = 7.71, N = 107) with status_explanation = "df's are very different", while the subjective scores are intermediate (replicated_instructor_code = 0.75, replicated_report_code = 0.5, adjudicated_replication_code = 0.75). As Boyce et al. (2023, Section 4.3.5) explain, raw_data.csv records only one statistical comparison whereas the subjective score reflects the broader pattern of results in the report. Without the primary report, it cannot be determined from primary evidence whether the 0.75 rating reflects mixed results across multiple tested outcomes ('mixed') or confirmation of the focal effect discounted for the degrees-of-freedom/modeling discrepancy ('successful'). Thus, the categorical outcome is undeterminable.
